arc: hook (title + pointer) → reveal (dock click) → feature: record → feature: layouts → feature: 3D angles + export → proof (published page) → logo + cta

scenes.title: Per-letter colour-wave title with a riding pointer
scenes.summary: On pure white, "Introducing Prequel" (124px, weight 500) resolves letter by letter out of a blur and a 46px drop, each glyph shifting yellow → green → ink as it lands, so the colour travels across the line as a wave. A macOS pointer rides the reveal front left to right, then glides down-left to rest near the left edge at dock height. The whole line launches upward out of frame in the last 14 frames while the pointer stays put to carry the cut.
scenes.build: Hand-rolled per-char spans: stagger() with each=1.2 and duration=16 drives opacity, blur, translateY and an RGB mix() through two colour stops. The pointer's x is a linear interpolate matched to the stagger's front so it stays on the newest letter. Uses the shared Cursor component (components/Cursor.tsx) and brand tokens.
scenes.reuse: Borrow for any 'Introducing X' cold open where a cursor will drive the next scene: swap LINE, the three colour stops and TEXT_L/TEXT_R for the new line width. The REST_X/REST_Y parking spot only matters if your next scene opens with the pointer at that spot. Don't copy the Prequel yellow/green unless it's your brand.

scenes.title: macOS dock pan with magnification, click to launch
scenes.summary: A frosted-glass macOS dock of 14 real app icons (Chrome, Figma, Notion, Spotify, Sublime, GitHub, Linear, Framer, Telegram, Prequel, Obsidian, Discord, X, Gmail) rises over a photo wallpaper. The pointer leads, the camera pans right across the dock, icons swell under the pointer like real dock magnification, a dark "Prequel" tooltip appears, the pointer clicks and the Prequel icon does one launch hop. The whole dock then drops out of frame.
scenes.build: <Camera world={2}> pans from x 0.25 to the Prequel slot; the cursor lives in world space and shares the camera's inOutCubic window so its screen path stays monotonic. Magnification is a smoothstep of horizontal pointer distance, gated by vertical distance to the dock's live position. The tray is a FrostedBackdrop (blurred, world-registered copy of the wallpaper) from components/desktop.tsx; pointer is components/Cursor.tsx.
scenes.reuse: Use whenever a product should be 'found and opened' from the desktop: swap the APPS icon list and which index is your app (PQ), the tooltip text and the wallpaper. Also works as an ecosystem / 'lives next to the tools you use' beat. Don't ship third-party logos you have no right to show; the Prequel icon is brand-specific.

scenes.title: Recording toolbar demo with mode tooltips and face-cam pop
scenes.summary: A dark frosted recording bar drops onto the desktop: close button, three capture-mode buttons, a "Camera" toggle and a "MacBook Pro Microp…" mic source. The pointer clicks through the modes as tooltips name each one ("Record Entire Screen", "Record a Window", "Record an Area") and the blue active pill slides after each click. It clicks Camera: the icon flips on, the dot turns green, the bar slides down and a rounded face-cam video preview springs in above it; the mic level dot then pulses amber. Everything swells and blurs away at the end.
scenes.build: Static <Camera> on the world from scene 2; the bar is absolutely positioned controls (lucide Monitor/AppWindow/Square/VideoOff/Mic) with per-control ring highlights interpolated in and out. Pointer path is one multi-keyframe interpolate with EASE_MOVE plus cursorDynamics() for bank/stretch and click dips; the preview is a <Video> with a bouncy spring. Exit scale/blur constants (OUT_SCALE, OUT_BLUR) are shared with scene 4 via components/desktop.tsx.
scenes.reuse: Borrow the pattern of a cursor stepping through toolbar controls with a tooltip naming each action, for any app with a mode picker or settings bar. Swap labels, icons and the face-cam clip. The scale-and-blur exit is a good handoff into a darker editor scene. The face-cam clip asset is a placeholder; replace it.

scenes.title: Layout picker morphing screen + camera between five layouts
scenes.summary: The desktop darkens and blurs, and a browser-window recording with a rounded face-cam appears centre stage above a frosted picker of five layout tiles. The pointer clicks tile after tile and the two rectangles glide into each layout: Side by side, Stacked, Camera focus (face-cam full frame, screen as a small inset), then back to Screen. The picker sinks away at the end, leaving the window to carry the cut.
scenes.build: Every layout is the same two rectangles, so LAYOUTS is a table of ten numbers (+ cam opacity) and each change is a lerp driven by interpolate over 24 frames; z-order flips mid-morph. Tiles draw their own mini diagram from the same numbers scaled by TILE_SCALE. BrowserWindow (components/BrowserWindow.tsx) is drawn at a fixed 1200x675 and scaled, so it never reflows; Cursor + cursorDynamics for the pointer.
scenes.reuse: The 'table of rectangles + lerp between rows' trick is the thing to steal: use it for any layout switcher, template picker or responsive-layout demo. Swap the contents of the two rectangles (screenshot, video, cards) and the number of layouts. The browser screenshot and face-cam footage are placeholders.

scenes.title: Preset dock swings a window through 3D angles, then Export blast
scenes.summary: The browser window from the previous scene sits on a dark blurred desktop while a preset dock of five tiles (each a tiny card tilted to its own preset) pops up below. The pointer clicks presets and the window swings in 3D to a right-facing angle, then a 'Hero' tilt, while the camera eases slightly in. The preset dock sinks, an action dock with Edit, Share and a green Export button rises, the pointer clicks Export and the window rushes the lens, un-tilting as it grows, into a near-black frame.
scenes.build: VIEWS holds rx/ry/rz/z/scale per preset; the window is a CSS perspective container with rotateX/Y/Z, and Z depth is applied as an equivalent scale (zoomOf) because a real translateZ inside <Camera> would rasterise stale. Docks live in <Overlay> so the camera move doesn't drag them. The export 'blast' multiplies scale by up to 7.5x while unwinding the angles, with a #0f0f0f flash matching the next scene's page colour.
scenes.reuse: Borrow for any 'pick a look / style preset' demo or to show a screenshot from cinematic angles; swap the VIEWS table and the window contents. The click-to-blast-into-frame ending is a strong handoff into a result screen; match the flash colour to your next scene's background.

scenes.title: Published on a dark video page, counters tick, logo burst
scenes.summary: A dark video-platform page fades up: a player shows the exported recording still swinging gently in 3D with a face-cam bubble and a red scrubber advancing, titled "Introducing Prequel — cinematic screen recordings", channel "Prequel" with "2.4K subscribers", likes counting 1,046 → 2,418 and views 11,842 → 18,630 ("2 days ago"), and an up-next shelf of thumbnails. The camera slowly pushes in. Then the page dims, the Prequel app icon rises to centre, the pointer clicks it and a white circle bursts out from under the mark to fill the frame.
scenes.build: Page furniture is hand-placed divs + lucide icons with staggered rise() entrances; the player's content reuses BrowserWindow under sine-driven rotateX/Y/Z with mismatched periods so it never loops visibly. CountText for both counters. The closing dim, white circle burst and logo sit in <Overlay> so the <Camera> push doesn't move them.
scenes.reuse: Use as the 'and it's out there / people are watching' payoff after a creation demo; swap title, channel name, counts and thumbnails. The click-the-logo-to-burst-white move is a reusable handoff into a white end card. The page imitates a well-known video site's layout with a generic red play mark; don't add a real platform's logo or name.

scenes.title: App icon end card: tagline clears, URL takes its place
scenes.summary: On white, the Prequel app icon (picked up centred from the previous scene) eases up while a faint orange-to-magenta glow breathes behind it. "Create Cinematic Screen Recordings" blurs up word by word, then "Made for Apple Silicon" in muted grey. Both clear at frame 120, the icon settles lower and "prequel.sh" resolves character by character beneath it as the last frame.
scenes.build: AbsoluteFill with an absolutely positioned icon whose y is a sum of lift, settle and a sine drift; a radial-gradient div behind it pulses via interpolate. Three TextAnimation blocks: blurUp by word with a hand-placed exit {at:120}, fadeUp by word, and blurUp by char for the URL (no exit; it is the final hold).
scenes.reuse: A clean light end card for any app launch: swap the icon, tagline, sub-line and URL, and the glow colours. Keep the 'copy clears, URL replaces it' sequencing. Mark position at frame 0 must match whatever your previous scene hands off.
